cases.caseId: live session deletion denies next private operation despite earlier success

links.scope: After a previous successful operation, deleting the exact current session causes the next request to return UNAUTHORIZED. This observes a fresh-session consequence, not every provider read/cache/cookie branch.
The deleted-session fixture observes the absent-session denial path only; malformed, expired and provider-unavailable paths remain separate.

cases.caseId: session revoked during actual startup queue is reread before business admission

links.scope: Revocation while actual startup is blocked yields UNAUTHORIZED and leaves the exact claim/audit/ledger snapshot unchanged. Does not establish all transaction ordering or RLS clauses.

The constructed runtime observes session deletion before business admission after its startup wait. This is a narrow consequence of the verifier binding, not proof of every constructor argument or provider contract.

cases.caseId: four-operation capacity rejects fifth before additional purpose pools and close drains owned work

links.scope: Four blocked operations have four actual data and four identity sessions; a fifth returns its original operation ID as indeterminate without increasing the observed session count. No general timing or pool-options claim.

After explicit close, the four owned pending requests settle indeterminate with their IDs, no audit is present, and the next request is refused. Session drain is retained in the frozen program but is a helper premise, not an independently selected assertion here.

cases.caseId: current role downgrade blocks prior administrator replay for another target

links.scope: A formerly-admin current actor changed to staff cannot replay an assignment to another target; exact SELF_ASSIGNMENT_ONLY is observed. Does not prove all actor predicates, locks or role cases.

cases.caseId: legacy replay returns durable result without duplicate audit or notification and aliases conflict

links.scope: Same legacy-admin UUID replays with unchanged state and one notice; changing the literal legacy entry yields OPERATION_CONFLICT. Other fingerprint fields and stored projection branches remain unqualified.

cases.caseId: legacy admin commits assignment audit ledger and independent notification using restricted purposes

links.scope: This legacy-admin write sets the requested staff while preserving the prior assignedAt and assignedById. The full UPDATE predicate/CAS/RETURNING and arbitrary column nonmutation are not inferred.
One audit has the supplied bounded IP and explicitly nonauthoritative observation flag for this successful legacy assignment. Full audit payload, rollback and every observation field remain separate.

A completed legacy assignment produces one notice with the expected target, tenant, title and claim URL. This does not prove the complete insertion predicate/conflict behavior, prior ledger gates, verified email or external delivery.

cases.caseId: admin eligible noop preserves terminal case and emits neither audit nor notification

links.scope: Eligible same-target legacy-admin request on the explicitly resolved fixture succeeds unchanged, preserves claim/audit and creates only its result row with no notice after drain. No claim about other eligibility or lifecycle branches.

cases.caseId: staff omitted target assigns current actor and explicit null clears assignment timestamps

links.scope: The omitted staff target resolves to the current staff actor, observed in stored assignee/assigner. Complete actor/current-tenant authority and explicit malformed cases remain separate.

Explicit null clears assignee, assignedAt and assignedById after this self assignment, with two audits total. Does not qualify complete UPDATE predicates, updatedAt clock authority, CAS or returning branches.
